about: A dream-test in an underground cavern. You wake at the foot of an endless stair and must prove yourself to an old wizard. A sword in a rock, a land of shadow and a hooded duelist who mirrors you are the first trials.

done.why: I had seen enough of the prose to judge it. The duel was a wall, and I left while exploring after my first death.

ending.what: None. I died once to the hooded duelist and was revived at the stair by the old man. I did not find the wizard.

moments.note: Walking south into the dark offered the classic grue warning.
Walking west into the mist turns you back, and the description is lovely.
The sword I had not taken appeared in my hand, glowing, when the figure showed up.
The duel repeated, and attacks were called feeble with no hint of what else to try.
I died, and the old man's revival scene was a strong passage.
After respawning, I tried to attack again and was told there was nothing to see.

wished: A hint on how to beat or avoid the duelist besides swinging blindly.
To read the runes on the sword.

lines.line: the way light does in dreams, and it throws your shadow several ways at once.
lines.why: It sets the dream mood early.

lines.line: a hilt worn to the shape of a hand, which, when you close yours on it, turns out to be yours.
lines.why: The best sentence I read. It is intimate and hints at the theme.

lines.line: the mist comes down over it thicker with every step, until you cannot see the ground you are walking on and have to turn back to find it.
lines.why: A refusal written as an experience.

lines.line: standing the way you stand and holding its sword the way you hold yours, which you had not noticed you did until now.

fun.why: The prose and the duel's premise were fun. The repetitive fight and an unclear route to winning it dragged.

engagement.why: I was drawn in by the descriptions, but the duel stalled me.

difficulty.why: The duel gave no sign of what works. It felt too hard, or I missed the trick.

interestingness.why: The doppelganger duel and the rock-bound sword are good ideas. The old man's revival frames death as part of the test.

prose.why: The rewritten descriptions are vivid and precise, and they sit beside terse classic-style lines. The voice is uneven between rooms, and the combat text repeats.
